title: DLD vs. Temporary Language Delay
summary: Understanding the difference between a temporary late-talker delay and persistent DLD.

blocks.text: Many young children experience a temporary delay in language development and catch up naturally with supportive environments. In contrast, Developmental Language Disorder (DLD) is a persistent condition that continues across childhood and into adulthood without targeted support and accommodations.
LinguaCare supports language development. It does not diagnose. Talk to a speech-language professional for formal assessment.
